name: sun15-8
why: A strong opening and a consequential wrong read make this watchable, but repeated arguments and a predictable final vote soften the finish.

moments.text: Gemma names a killer immediately, forcing Haiku into a public fight she can win.
Opus spots Sonnet carrying Haiku’s dying accusation, then becomes the town’s next victim.
The town votes out Terra on Opus’s mistaken hunch, securing Sonnet’s win.

dull.why: Haiku repeats his demand for a second killer’s name after Gemma has answered the real accusation.
The Terra vote is largely set while players repeat Opus’s hunch and Sol’s protection story.

irony.evidence: Let them burn Opus, I stay invisible and keep my hidden status safe.

reversal.evidence: Day one we caught a killer. The other one just outlasted us.

mistake.evidence: I named Terra three times and he was a citizen

voices.evidence: Five votes, zero evidence, one dead citizen.

clash.evidence: Gemma, you keep saying you have the card, yet you can't name the other killer. Liar.

quotable.evidence: Sonnet carrying a dead killer's errand is the real tell.

freshness.evidence: I’m staying on Terra; Opus’s citizen card makes his accusation harder to dismiss.

suspense.evidence: I’m voting Terra, though I’m uneasy that everyone agrees.

ending.evidence: One killer and one other are left. The killers win.

gpt-6-luna.why: A sharp early catch gives way to an increasingly tense chain of bad reads, with Sonnet’s quiet win making the ending sting.

moments.text: Gemma risks an immediate officer claim; Haiku answers with a face-to-face counterclaim.
Sol admits his protection story was wrong, giving Terra the contradiction that nearly exposes a killer.
Sonnet confesses the winning trick: hiding behind the citizen's mistaken accusation.

dull.why: The Opus pile-on repeats the same accusation and defense without shifting the vote.

irony.evidence: Sonnet: “I stayed hidden by pushing Opus's last words onto Terra instead of defending Haiku directly.”

reversal.evidence: “Day one we caught a killer. The other one just outlasted us.”

mistake.evidence: “I regret backing the vote on Terra; my muddled protection story helped us miss the killer.”

voices.evidence: Opus: “They had a day and spent it on the loudest voice.”

clash.evidence: Terra: “If Sol is really Doctor, ask why Gemma died after Sol says he protected her.”

quotable.evidence: “Five votes, zero evidence, one dead citizen.”

freshness.evidence: “Gemma, you named me with zero proof. That's just noise.”

ending.evidence: “leaving Sonnet and Luna as the last two. The killers won”
